points: "Im ya'amod Moshe u'Shmuel lefanai": even if Moshe and Shmuel, two of the greatest nevi'im, stood up for this nation, Hashem would not change His plan.
Yirmiyahu turns inward: "Oy li imi" — woe to me, mother, that you bore me; everyone curses me. He is a broken man.
Hashem doesn't promise it will be easy, but promises to save him from his enemies. And in the end Yirmiyahu is protected, even by the invading army.
The Malbim: a navi normally needs simcha to receive prophecy. Yirmiyahu was so sad that Hashem gave him joy in the moment the prophecy came, and then he went back to his darkness.
The Radak: the end of the chapter is Hashem telling Yirmiyahu he went too far in how he spoke to Him. If he does teshuvah, Hashem will keep him safe.
